question: 46. A function $f$ from a set $A$ into a set $B$ is a rule which assigns to each element $x$ in $A$, a unique (one and only one) element (denoted by $f(x)$) in $B$. A function $f$ from $A$ into $B$ is called an onto function, if for each $y$ in $B$ there is some element $x$ in $A$, such that $f(x)=y$. Now suppose that $A=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ and $B=\{1,2,3\}$. Determine the total number of onto functions from $A$ into $B$.
